course.title: Sports Coaching Basics
course.tagline: Coach a team: drills, tactics and keeping players motivated.

days.title: What does a sports coach do?
days.goal: Learn what a coach does and what makes a good one.

video.title: Intro To Coaching Video

steps: Watch the video and write down 3 jobs a coach does.
A coach teaches skills, plans practice and keeps players safe.
Write one sentence that says what a coach is in your own words.
Ask a friend what they want from a coach.
days.task: Write what a coach does in 5 lines.
days.challenge: Explain what a coach does to a friend in 1 minute.

quiz.q: What is the main job of a sports coach?
options: Teach skills, plan practice and keep players safe
quiz.explain: A coach teaches, plans and protects players.

quiz.q: What makes a good coach?
options: Patience, clear words and care for players
quiz.explain: Patience and clear words build good players.

quiz.q: What should a coach do first?
options: Learn the players' names and levels
quiz.explain: Knowing players helps you coach each one.

days.title: Plan your first practice
days.goal: Learn to plan a simple 60-minute practice.

video.title: One touch pass activation

steps: A good practice has 4 parts: warm-up, skill 1, skill 2, small game.
Give each part a time: 10, 15, 15, 15 minutes, plus a 5-minute huddle.
Write your plan on one page.
Keep talks short: about 30 seconds each.
days.task: Write a 60-minute practice plan on one page.
days.challenge: Time each part of your plan.

quiz.q: What are the 4 parts of a practice?
quiz.explain: A good practice warms up, teaches and plays.

quiz.q: How long should a practice be?
quiz.explain: Sixty minutes is enough for young players.

quiz.q: How long should coach talks be?
quiz.explain: Short talks keep players moving.

days.title: Warm up with a game
days.goal: Learn warm-up games that get players moving.

video.title: One Touch Passing Drill

steps: Try tag: one player chases, others dribble away.
Try red light, green light with a ball.
Keep everyone moving: no long lines.
End the warm-up with a quick stretch.
days.task: Run a 10-minute warm-up game with friends.
days.challenge: Teach the warm-up game to a fellow coach.

quiz.q: Why warm up with a game?
quiz.explain: Fun warm-ups get players moving happily.

quiz.q: Why avoid long lines?
options: Lines waste time and bore players
quiz.explain: No lines means more touches on the ball.

quiz.q: What should a warm-up end with?
quiz.explain: A stretch after warming up prepares muscles.

days.title: Teach passing simply
days.goal: Learn to teach a simple inside-of-the-foot pass.

video.title: Dribbling and Reaction Drill for Youth Soccer

steps: Show the pass: inside of the foot, ankle locked, follow through.
Let players pass in pairs, 10 passes each.
Say one cue: toes up.
Praise good passes out loud.
days.task: Teach the pass to a friend using one cue.
days.challenge: Practise 20 passes in pairs.

quiz.q: What part of the foot passes best?
quiz.explain: The inside gives the most control.

quiz.q: What should the ankle do?
quiz.explain: A locked ankle makes a clean pass.

quiz.q: What is a good coaching cue?
options: One short hint like toes up
quiz.explain: One short cue is easy to remember.

days.title: Teach dribbling simply
days.goal: Learn to teach dribbling with small touches.

video.title: Soccer Drill: Passing, Trapping, Turning, Vision and Shooting

steps: Show dribbling: small touches, ball close to the feet.
Set up cone gates and let players dribble through.
Say one cue: keep the ball close.
Let players try at their own speed.
days.task: Teach dribbling to a friend using one cue.
days.challenge: Dribble through 5 cone gates.

quiz.q: What is dribbling?
options: Moving the ball with small touches
quiz.explain: Dribbling keeps the ball close while moving.

quiz.q: Why keep the ball close?
options: So you can change direction fast
quiz.explain: A close ball lets you turn and pass fast.

quiz.q: What is a cone gate?
options: Two cones that make a small goal to dribble through
quiz.explain: Gates give players a target to aim through.

days.title: Teach shooting simply
days.goal: Learn to teach a simple shot on goal.

video.title: Top Soccer Fundamentals Explained | Basic Soccer Skills

steps: Show shooting: plant foot next to the ball, lock ankle, follow through.
Let players shoot at a small goal from close in.
Say one cue: plant foot next to the ball.
Praise every shot on target.
days.task: Teach shooting to a friend using one cue.
days.challenge: Take 10 shots at a small goal.

quiz.q: Where should the plant foot go?
options: Next to the ball, pointing at the goal
quiz.explain: The plant foot next to the ball aims the shot.

quiz.q: What should the ankle do when shooting?
quiz.explain: A locked ankle makes a clean shot.

quiz.q: What should you praise?
quiz.explain: Praising good tries builds confidence.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 1: Run your first practice
days.goal: Put week 1 together: run a full 60-minute practice.

video.title: Soccer Training for Kids at Home: Episode 5

steps: Use your plan: warm-up game, passing, dribbling, small game.
Run it with friends acting as players.
Keep talks to 30 seconds.
Ask players what was fun and what was hard.
days.task: Run your first practice and write how it went.
days.challenge: Run the practice without looking at your notes.

quiz.q: What should your first practice have?
options: Warm-up, two skills and a small game
quiz.explain: A full practice warms up, teaches and plays.

quiz.q: How long should talks be?
quiz.explain: Short talks keep players moving.

quiz.q: What should you ask at the end?
options: What was fun and what was hard
quiz.explain: Asking players helps you improve.

project.title: Run your first practice
project.brief: Run a full 60-minute practice with friends as players: warm-up game, passing, dribbling, small game, and ask what was fun and hard.

days.title: Coach different ages
days.goal: Learn how coaching changes with age.

video.title: Soccer Training for Kids at Home: Episode 6

steps: Young players (5-7): focus on fun and touches on the ball.
Older players (8-12): add simple tactics and teamwork.
Teen players: add fitness and game plans.
Write one practice idea for each age.
days.task: Write one practice idea for each age group.
days.challenge: Coach a game for young players this week.

quiz.q: What should young players focus on?
options: Fun and touches on the ball
quiz.explain: Young players learn through fun and touches.

quiz.q: What can older players add?
quiz.explain: Older players can learn tactics and teamwork.

quiz.q: Why change coaching by age?
quiz.explain: Age-matched coaching helps every player grow.

days.title: Keep players safe
days.goal: Learn the safety rules every coach must know.

video.title: Full Football Training Session 01 | Animated Drills & Games with Audio Guide

steps: Check the field for holes and glass before practice.
Make sure players drink water.
Stop play if a player is hurt.
Know where the first aid kit is.
days.task: Check a field for dangers before practice.
days.challenge: Find the first aid kit at your field.

quiz.q: What should you check before practice?
options: The field for holes and glass
quiz.explain: A safe field prevents injuries.

quiz.q: Why make players drink water?
options: To replace sweat and prevent heat problems
quiz.explain: Water keeps players safe in heat.

quiz.q: What should you do if a player is hurt?
options: Tell them to run it off
Stop play and check on them
quiz.explain: Stopping play keeps the hurt player safe.

days.title: Motivate your players
days.goal: Learn simple ways to keep players excited.

video.title: Fun Drills For Kids | U5, U6, U7, U8, U9 | 👇*Free Session Plans*👇| Football Coaching for Kids

steps: Praise effort, not just goals.
Give every player a job in the game.
Celebrate small wins out loud.
Ask players what they enjoyed.
days.task: Praise 3 players for effort today.
days.challenge: Give every player a job in your next game.

quiz.q: What should you praise?
quiz.explain: Praising effort builds hard workers.

quiz.q: Why give every player a job?
quiz.explain: A job for everyone builds teamwork.

quiz.q: Why celebrate small wins?
quiz.explain: Small wins build confidence.

days.title: Teach teamwork simply
days.goal: Learn to teach players to play together.

video.title: Intro To Coaching Video

steps: Play small games: 3v3 or 4v4.
Say one cue: look up before you pass.
Praise a good pass more than a good goal.
Let players make mistakes and try again.
days.task: Run a 3v3 game with friends.
days.challenge: Praise 3 good passes in the game.

quiz.q: Why play small games?
options: Every player touches the ball more
quiz.explain: Small games give every player more touches.

quiz.q: What should players do before passing?
quiz.explain: Looking up finds teammates.

quiz.q: Why praise passes more than goals?
quiz.explain: Passing is teamwork in action.

days.title: Plan a season
days.goal: Learn to plan a whole season, week by week.

video.title: One touch pass activation

steps: A season has weeks: early weeks teach basics, later weeks add tactics.
Write a simple plan: one skill per week.
Add one game each week to test the skill.
Keep the plan on one page.
days.task: Write a 4-week season plan.
days.challenge: Share your plan with a fellow coach.

quiz.q: How should a season be planned?
options: One skill per week, basics first
quiz.explain: One skill a week builds steadily.

quiz.q: Why test skills in a game each week?
options: Games show if the skill works
quiz.explain: Games test learning in real play.

quiz.q: How long should a season plan be?
quiz.explain: A one-page plan is easy to follow.

days.title: Handle parents well
days.goal: Learn to talk to parents kindly and clearly.

video.title: One Touch Passing Drill

steps: Tell parents the practice times and what to bring.
Explain your playing-time rule before the first game.
Thank parents for bringing their children.
Listen to concerns calmly and reply the next day if needed.
days.task: Write a short welcome message to parents.
days.challenge: Practise explaining your playing-time rule.

quiz.q: What should you tell parents first?
options: Practice times and what to bring
quiz.explain: Clear facts help parents plan.

quiz.q: Why explain playing time before the first game?
options: So everyone knows the rule is fair
quiz.explain: A clear rule before the game prevents arguments.

quiz.q: What should you do with a concern?
options: Listen calmly and reply the next day if needed
quiz.explain: Calm listening builds trust.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 2: Your season plan
days.goal: Put week 2 together: write a full season plan.

video.title: Dribbling and Reaction Drill for Youth Soccer

steps: Write a 6-week plan: one skill per week.
Add a warm-up game and a small game each week.
Add your playing-time rule.
Share the plan with a fellow coach for feedback.
days.task: Write your 6-week season plan.
days.challenge: Get feedback from a fellow coach.

quiz.q: How many weeks should your plan have?
quiz.explain: Six weeks is a good first season plan.

quiz.q: What should each week have?
options: One skill, a warm-up game and a small game
quiz.explain: Each week teaches and plays.

quiz.q: Why get feedback on your plan?
options: Another coach may spot what you missed
quiz.explain: Feedback makes plans better.

project.title: Your season plan
project.brief: Write a 6-week season plan with one skill per week, a warm-up game and a small game each week, and your playing-time rule.
checks: Each week has a warm-up game
Each week has a small game
Got feedback from a fellow coach

days.title: Teach defence simply
days.goal: Learn to teach simple defending.

video.title: Soccer Drill: Passing, Trapping, Turning, Vision and Shooting

steps: Show defending: stay between the attacker and your goal.
Say one cue: stay goalside.
Play 1v1 games to practise.
Praise good defending out loud.
days.task: Teach defending to a friend using one cue.
days.challenge: Play 1v1 defending games.

quiz.q: What does goalside mean?
options: Between the attacker and your goal
quiz.explain: Goalside is the safe defending spot.

quiz.q: Why play 1v1 games?
options: They teach defending in real situations
quiz.explain: One-on-one games teach real defending.

quiz.q: What should you praise in defence?
quiz.explain: Praising good position builds defenders.

days.title: Teach goalkeeping basics
days.goal: Learn the basics of goalkeeping.

video.title: Top Soccer Fundamentals Explained | Basic Soccer Skills

steps: Show the ready position: knees bent, hands up, on toes.
Show catching: hands in a W shape for high balls.
Show diving: step, fall sideways, land softly.
Let every player try goalkeeping.
days.task: Teach the ready position to a friend.
days.challenge: Practise catching a ball in a W shape.

quiz.q: What is the goalkeeper's ready position?
options: Knees bent, hands up, on toes
quiz.explain: Ready position lets the keeper react fast.

quiz.q: What shape should hands make for a high catch?
quiz.explain: A W shape catches the ball safely.

quiz.q: Why let every player try goalkeeping?
options: So they respect the job and learn the skills
Only one player should do it
quiz.explain: Trying goalkeeping builds respect and skills.

days.title: Game day: what to do
days.goal: Learn how to run a game day smoothly.

video.title: Soccer Training for Kids at Home: Episode 5

steps: Arrive early and check the field.
Warm players up with a game.
Share the playing-time plan before the game.
After the game, praise effort and ask what was fun.
days.task: Write a game-day checklist.
days.challenge: Use the checklist at your next game.

quiz.q: What should you do first on game day?
options: Arrive early and check the field
quiz.explain: Arriving early keeps game day smooth.

quiz.q: When should you share the playing-time plan?
quiz.explain: Sharing before the game is fair.

quiz.q: What should you do after the game?
options: Praise effort and ask what was fun
quiz.explain: Praise and fun keep players coming back.

days.title: Fair playing time
days.goal: Learn to give every player fair time.

video.title: Soccer Training for Kids at Home: Episode 6

steps: Write your rule before the season: equal time for all.
Split players into groups and swap them regularly.
Track minutes with a simple sheet.
Tell parents the rule before the first game.
days.task: Write your playing-time rule.
days.challenge: Make a simple minutes tracker.

quiz.q: Why give equal playing time?
options: It is fair and keeps all players growing
quiz.explain: Fair time grows every player.

quiz.q: How do you track playing time?
quiz.explain: A sheet makes fair time real.

quiz.q: When should you tell parents the rule?
quiz.explain: Telling early prevents arguments.

days.title: Deal with a tough game
days.goal: Learn what to do when your team loses badly.

video.title: Full Football Training Session 01 | Animated Drills & Games with Audio Guide

steps: Stay calm and praise effort.
Ask players what they learned.
Pick one thing to practise next week.
Remind players that losing is part of learning.
days.task: Write 3 kind words for a team after a loss.
days.challenge: Practise saying them out loud.

quiz.q: What should you do after a big loss?
quiz.explain: Calm praise after a loss builds strength.

quiz.q: What should you ask players after a loss?
quiz.explain: Asking what they learned turns loss into growth.

quiz.q: Why remind players losing is normal?
options: It keeps them from fearing failure
quiz.explain: Normalising loss builds brave players.

days.title: Fitness for young players
days.goal: Learn simple fitness that suits young players.

video.title: Fun Drills For Kids | U5, U6, U7, U8, U9 | 👇*Free Session Plans*👇| Football Coaching for Kids

steps: Use games for fitness: tag, relay races, small games.
Keep fitness fun, not boring laps.
Add 5 minutes of running games to practice.
Let players rest and drink water.
days.task: Add a running game to your next practice.
days.challenge: Run a relay race with friends.

quiz.q: Why use games for fitness?
quiz.explain: Fun games build fitness without boredom.

quiz.q: Why not make young players run laps?
options: Laps are boring and tire them out
quiz.explain: Games build fitness better than laps.

quiz.q: What should players do after fitness games?
quiz.explain: Rest and water keep players safe.

days.title: PROJECT WEEK 3: Coach a full game
days.goal: Put week 3 together: coach a full small-sided game.

video.title: Intro To Coaching Video

steps: Plan the game: teams, playing-time swaps, one skill focus.
Warm players up, then play 3v3 or 4v4.
Use your playing-time tracker.
After the game, praise effort and ask what was fun.
days.task: Coach a full game with friends.
days.challenge: Use your playing-time tracker in the game.

quiz.q: What should you plan before a game?
options: Teams, swaps and one skill focus
quiz.explain: A plan keeps game day smooth.

quiz.q: Why use a playing-time tracker?
options: So every player gets fair time
quiz.explain: A tracker makes fair time real.

quiz.q: What should you do after the game?
options: Praise effort and ask what was fun
quiz.explain: Praise and fun keep players coming back.

project.title: Coach a full game
project.brief: Coach a full small-sided game with a plan, fair playing-time swaps tracked on a sheet, and praise for effort after.

days.title: Review your season
days.goal: Look back at your season and learn from it.

video.title: One touch pass activation

steps: Read your plans from weeks 1 to 3.
List 3 things that went well.
List 1 thing to improve next season.
Write one fix for that thing.
days.task: List 3 things that went well this season.
days.challenge: Write one fix for next season.

quiz.q: Why review your season?
options: To learn what worked and what to fix
quiz.explain: Reviewing makes you a better coach.

quiz.q: What should you do with a weak spot?
options: Fix it with one small change
quiz.explain: One small fix improves next season.

quiz.q: What is a sign your season went well?
quiz.explain: Fun and growth mean a good season.

days.title: Keep coaching: your next season
days.goal: Plan your next season and keep growing as a coach.

video.title: One Touch Passing Drill

steps: Pick one new skill to learn as a coach.
Ask players and parents for feedback.
Join a coaching course or group.
Write your next season plan.
days.task: Ask one player for feedback.
days.challenge: Write your next season plan.

quiz.q: How do coaches keep growing?
options: By learning, asking feedback and trying new things
quiz.explain: Learning and feedback grow coaches.

quiz.q: Why ask players for feedback?
options: They know what helped them most
quiz.explain: Player feedback shows what works.

quiz.q: What is a good next step?
options: Join a coaching course or group
quiz.explain: A course or group builds new skills.

days.title: Teach a new coach
days.goal: Teach someone else what you learned.

video.title: Dribbling and Reaction Drill for Youth Soccer

steps: Show them how to plan a practice.
Show them the warm-up game.
Show them one cue for passing.
Ask them how they felt after.
days.task: Teach practice planning to one person.
days.challenge: Show a new coach your warm-up game.

quiz.q: Why teach a new coach?
options: Teaching helps you learn it better
quiz.explain: Teaching locks in your own learning.

quiz.q: What is the first thing to teach?
quiz.explain: Planning is the base of coaching.

quiz.q: Why ask how they felt?
options: So you know if the teaching helped
quiz.explain: Feedback shows what works.

days.title: Teach catching and throwing
days.goal: Learn to teach simple catching and throwing.

video.title: Soccer Drill: Passing, Trapping, Turning, Vision and Shooting

steps: Show throwing: step forward with the other foot.
Show catching: hands ready, watch the ball.
Start close together and throw gently.
Move further apart as players get better.
Say one cue: watch the ball.
Praise every catch.
days.task: Teach catching to a friend.
days.challenge: Play catch for 10 minutes.

quiz.q: What should you do when throwing?
options: Step forward with the other foot
Throw as hard as you can
quiz.explain: Stepping forward gives the throw power and aim.

quiz.q: What should your hands do when catching?
options: Be ready and watch the ball
quiz.explain: Ready hands and watching eyes catch the ball.

quiz.q: Why start close together?
options: So catching is easy at first
quiz.explain: Close throws build confidence first.

days.title: Coach a player who is struggling
days.goal: Learn to help a player who finds it hard.

video.title: Top Soccer Fundamentals Explained | Basic Soccer Skills

steps: Notice the player and talk to them kindly.
Break the skill into a smaller step.
Let them practise the small step until it feels easy.
Praise every small win.
Pair them with a patient friend.
Check on them again next practice.
days.task: Write a plan to help a struggling player.
days.challenge: Use the plan with a real player.

quiz.q: What is the first step?
quiz.explain: Kind words open the door to help.

quiz.q: Why break the skill into a smaller step?
options: So it feels easy to do
quiz.explain: Small steps build confidence.

quiz.q: Why praise small wins?
quiz.explain: Small wins show the player they are growing.

days.title: Plan a fun end-of-season party
days.goal: Learn to plan a simple celebration for your team.

video.title: Soccer Training for Kids at Home: Episode 5

steps: Pick a date after the last game.
Ask players what food they like.
Plan one fun game, like a parents vs players match.
Give every player a small award.
Thank the parents and helpers.
Take a team photo.
days.task: Write a party plan for your team.
days.challenge: Share the plan with the team.

quiz.q: When should the party be?
quiz.explain: After the last game the whole team can celebrate.

quiz.q: What should every player get?
quiz.explain: An award for everyone celebrates every player.

quiz.q: Why plan a fun game?
quiz.explain: A fun game ends the season with joy.

days.title: Get ready for your capstone
days.goal: Review the whole course and prepare your final project.

video.title: Soccer Training for Kids at Home: Episode 6

steps: Read your notes from weeks 1 to 4.
List 5 coaching skills you learned.
Practise your capstone session once.
Write down any questions you still have.
days.task: List 5 coaching skills you learned.
days.challenge: Run your capstone session from memory.

quiz.q: What is the capstone?
options: A final project that shows what you learned
quiz.explain: The capstone is your final show of skill.

quiz.q: What should you review before the capstone?
options: Your notes from all four weeks
quiz.explain: Reviewing all weeks brings the course together.

quiz.q: How do you know you are ready?
options: You can run a full practice and a game safely
quiz.explain: Running a full session well shows you are ready.

days.title: Final practice day
days.goal: Practise your capstone once more, then rest.

video.title: Full Football Training Session 01 | Animated Drills & Games with Audio Guide

steps: Run your capstone practice one more time.
Check your plan, your time and your cues.
Fix anything that felt rushed.
Rest well tonight.
days.task: Run your capstone practice and time each part.
days.challenge: Fix one thing that felt rushed.

quiz.q: Why practise once more?
options: Practice makes the real run calm and smooth
quiz.explain: Practice turns worry into calm confidence.

quiz.q: What should you check after practice?
options: Your plan, your time and your cues
quiz.explain: Checking plan and time makes it smooth.

quiz.q: What should you do the night before?
quiz.explain: Good rest helps you do your best.

days.title: Capstone day: coach your team
days.goal: Show what you learned: coach a full practice and game.

video.title: Fun Drills For Kids | U5, U6, U7, U8, U9 | 👇*Free Session Plans*👇| Football Coaching for Kids

steps: Run your 60-minute practice from your plan.
Coach a small-sided game with fair playing time.
Use clear cues and praise effort.
Write a short report on how it went.
days.task: Coach your capstone practice and game, then write your report.
days.challenge: Hand in your report and celebrate.

quiz.q: What is the first step of your capstone?
quiz.explain: A warm-up game starts the session well.

quiz.q: What matters most in the capstone?
options: Clear cues, fair time and happy players
quiz.explain: Clear coaching and fair time show real skill.

quiz.q: What goes in your report?
options: What you did and what you learned
quiz.explain: A short report shows what you learned.

capstone.title: Coach your team
capstone.brief: Coach a full 60-minute practice from your plan and a small-sided game with fair playing time, clear cues and praise for effort, and write a short report.
deliverables: A short video or notes from the game
